dimensions.assessment: Affects state agencies administering CCDBG funds and state populations relying on program funding.
dimensions.evidence: If for a fiscal year the improper payment rate of a State is more than 5 percent... such State shall submit... a corrective action plan

dimensions.assessment: Introduces strict corrective action requirements and potential loss of program funding for states with persistent improper payment rates above 5 percent.
dimensions.evidence: such State shall be ineligible to receive funds under this subchapter unless such State demonstrates... that such State... will reduce such improper payment rate

dimensions.assessment: May result in the withholding or reallocation of federal block grant funds based on state error rates, but specific dollar amounts are not stated.
dimensions.evidence: ineligible to receive funds under this subchapter

dimensions.assessment: Amends section 658J of the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 to add improper payment thresholds and penalties.
dimensions.evidence: Section 658J of the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. 9858h) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory requirement governing ongoing state improper payment rates and eligibility.

missing_information: Current improper payment rates for individual states are not specified in the text.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a 5 percent improper payment threshold under the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act, requiring corrective action plans and imposing conditional ineligibility for states exceeding the rate for consecutive years.
